Severe Flooding Disrupts Banking Industry Operations Across Peru

A wave of severe flooding triggered by unseasonably intense rainfall has struck the banking industry’s own sites throughout Peru, forcing temporary branch closures, damaging corporate premises, and impacting hundreds of employees, according to industry officials and local unions.

As of Thursday, several banking firms, including leading national institutions such as Banco Soberano del Perú and FinanPeru, have reported direct impacts to their own branch networks and administrative offices in Lima, Cusco, and the northern coastal city of Trujillo. In some cases, floodwaters have inundated ground floors, damaging essential hardware, records, and security systems. At least 42 branches nationwide have suspended in-person services due to unsafe conditions, according to provisional data provided by the Asociación Bancaria Peruana (ABP).

“We are experiencing unprecedented flooding within our Lima headquarters. Water levels rose rapidly overnight, compromising vaults and IT infrastructure,” said Javier Arriaga, spokesperson for Banco Soberano del Perú. “Our contingency protocols are activated, but the situation remains fluid and could evolve quickly.”

Initial estimates from the ABP indicate that up to 15% of all bank-operated sites nationwide are facing some level of disruption, with urban centers hardest hit. The flooding has also forced the evacuation of roughly 900 industry employees from affected sites, with union representatives expressing concern for staff safety and the potential for longer-term displacement.

“We are in close communication with our members and the banking employers to ensure the safety of all workers,” said Juana Salazar, president of the Sindicato Nacional de Trabajadores Bancarios. “The immediate priority is to safeguard lives, but we are also pressing for clear plans to address lost workdays and the restoration of safe working environments.”

The ongoing event has hampered industry efforts to maintain regular in-person operations, with some firms attempting to reroute customers to undamaged branches. However, the ABP cautioned that the full extent of physical damage and service disruption is still being assessed as floodwaters have yet to recede in key areas.

“As the flooding continues, our member banks are focused on protecting their facilities, data, and personnel,” the ABP said in a statement. “We urge all staff and clients to follow official safety guidance while we work to restore normal operations.”

With meteorological forecasts predicting further rainfall in the coming days, banking industry officials are bracing for continued challenges and are coordinating closely with local authorities to monitor developments.
